To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the time series model-selection procedures are useful in suggesting a parsimonious final-form model for the confinements series; and (ii) the post-sample forecast performance of the confinements model is superior to the performance of the univariate models, and is also comparable with that of the IMPACT module.

(a) the IMPACT demographic module is based on the assumption of a linear relationship between the number of births and the number of women of child bearing age; (b) the IMPACT module's assumption of linearity is not supported by the data; (c) the IMPACT assumption that the number of births is linearly related to the number of women in the child bearing ages implies that the IMPACT module cannot be used to forecast births in Australia.

(1) the final-form models of births and first nuptial births are superior to the univariate models for forecasting births and first nupitals respectively; (2) the univariate models are superior to the final-form models in forecasting second and higher order nuptial births; and (3) the IMPACT module is superior to the final form models in forecasting births.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) What is the most appropriate model specification for forecasting Australian births?
the following questions: (1) What is the most appropriate dynamic specification for a demographic model?
the following questions: (1) Can the IMPACT demographic model be improved?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no clear winner in the contest between the IMPACT model, which is based on an econometric model, and the univariate models which are the outcome of a time-series analysis.
the IMPACT module is an excellent forecasting model for the short term.
the final-form models suggested in the paper are superior to the univariate models in forecasting confinements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IMPACT module, which uses the time series approach to select the final form model, performs better than the univariate ARMA models.
the final-form models are preferable for forecasting purposes.
the IMPACT module is a good forecasting model, but that the final form equations are not the most appropriate for forecasting purposes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a forecasting model should be based on a final-form equation which has been selected using an appropriate empirical model selection procedure, rather than an ad-hoc procedure such as IMPACT.
the IMPACT model's specification is not consistent with that implied by the Australian births time series.
the IMPACT module's demographic equations are not consistent with the data, in that they do not provide a good description of the data.
